sources.sentence: At the microphone, my mind had gone blank.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row7; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Suddenly be unable to recall what one knew or intended to say.
brief.meaningZh: 突然想不起本來知道或打算說的內容。
brief.grammar: my mind goes/went/has gone/had gone blank; possessive follows the person whose recall fails; a momentary experience, not a diagnosis.
brief.register: Common conversational idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示本來沒有準備、故意不答或記憶永久消失；需看當刻想不起甚麼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 短暫想不起不證明從未知道；也不同於明知答案但決定不說。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述短暫忘記的時點，並自然請求提示或片刻。

listening.en: I had practised the welcome, but when the first visitor asked my name, my mind went blank for a moment; looking at my badge helped me start again.
listening.zh: 我練過歡迎詞，但首位訪客問名字時，腦袋一時空白；看看名牌才幫我重新開始。
listening.promptZh: 哪個理解符合這段經歷？

options.en: The speaker briefly could not recall what to say, despite having prepared.
options.zh: 說話者雖有準備，仍短暫想不起要說甚麼。

options.en: The speaker deliberately kept the name secret while remembering it clearly.
options.zh: 說話者清楚記得名字，卻故意保密。

options.en: The badge was needed because no welcome had ever been prepared.
options.zh: 需用名牌，是因從未準備過歡迎詞。

options.en: The speaker forgot the visitor’s name after a long conversation.
options.zh: 長談之後，說話者忘了訪客的名字。

listening.explanationZh: had practised 保留準備；for a moment 及提示後再開始，支持短暫想不起，而非故意隱瞞。

reply.promptEn: Why did you look at your badge before starting again?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼重新開始前要看名牌？

options.en: My mind had gone blank, and it gave me a prompt.
options.zh: 我剛才腦袋空白，名牌給了提示。

options.en: I briefly could not bring the words to mind.
options.zh: 我一時想不起那些話。

options.en: The visitor’s first question caught me without a ready response.
options.zh: 訪客首個問題令我一時答不出。

options.en: I needed a reminder even though I had practised.
options.zh: 雖然練過，我仍需提示。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋需要提示，沒有改成從未準備或故意不答。

scene.promptZh: 討論時你明明記得作者名字，但刻意等一位較少發言的同伴先答，稍後再補充；沒有突然想不起內容。哪句較準確？

options.en: I chose to wait before answering; my mind had not gone blank.
options.zh: 我選擇稍等才回答；不是腦袋突然空白。

options.en: My mind went blank, so I could not recall the author’s name at that moment.
options.zh: 我腦袋突然空白，當刻想不起作者名字。

options.en: I needed someone to remind me of a name I could no longer remember.
options.zh: 我已記不起名字，需要別人提醒。

scene.explanationZh: 明確記得而刻意讓同伴先說，是發言選擇；沒有當刻無法想起的線索。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種情況最不宜用 my mind went blank 描述？

options.en: 知道答案，卻明確決定先讓別人回答。
練過內容，輪到自己時突然想不起開場。
一時想不起熟悉名稱，稍後靠提示記起。

contrast.explanationZh: 清楚知道而選擇不答，是發言決定，不是當刻無法想起。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴錄音時忘了熟悉的材料名稱，說「不是不想答，剛才想不起來」。你想讓她有機會重錄。哪句回應較好？

options.en: Your mind went blank for a moment; shall we pause and try that line again?
options.zh: 你剛才腦袋一時空白；我們停一下，再試那句好嗎？

options.en: That pause suggests you learned the ingredient’s name only after my prompt.
options.zh: 那次停頓顯示你是在我提示後才學會材料名字。

options.en: I will finish the line and move to the next ingredient; there is no need for you to retry that part.
options.zh: 我會說完那句，直接到下一項材料；你不用重試那部分。

dialogue.explanationZh: 她想有機會重錄，停一下再自己試最貼切；原已熟悉名稱，並非提示後才學會，也不需先代她說完。

speaking.en: My mind went blank when I tried to introduce myself, so I asked for a moment to gather my thoughts.
speaking.zh: 我想自我介紹時，腦袋突然空白，所以請對方給我片刻整理思緒。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述突然想不起來及自然請求。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友在介紹自己作品時說腦袋突然空白，想停一下自己再試，不想你替他答完。你想回覆，承認短暫想不起，讓他稍後選擇從哪裏重新開始。用一至兩句英文給支持。

examples.en: Your mind went blank for a moment; take your time, and I will not finish the answer for you. Would you like to restart with the title or another part when you are ready?
examples.zh: 你腦袋一時空白；慢慢來，我不會替你答完。準備好後，你想由標題還是另一部分重新開始？

examples.en: If your mind has gone blank, we can pause before you choose where to begin again. I can wait while you gather your thoughts.
examples.zh: 如果你腦袋突然空白，我們可先停，讓你選從哪裏再開始。我可以等你整理思緒。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認短暫想不起，提供停頓與選擇，尊重朋友想自己再試，不代答或迫他立即記起。

takeaways.en: His mind went blank during the introduction, but a glance at his notes helped him continue.
takeaways.zh: 介紹時他腦袋一時空白，但看一眼筆記便幫他繼續。

takeaways.en: My mind has gone blank about the title; could you tell me the author’s name as a clue?
takeaways.zh: 書名我一時想不起；可否告訴我作者名字作提示？

sources.sentence: My heart was racing before the interview.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row8; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Feel one’s heart beating very fast, often during fear or excitement.
brief.meaningZh: 感到心跳很快，常見於害怕或興奮的敘述。
brief.grammar: my/her heart is/was racing; race describes rapid beating here; context identifies the feeling, not the phrase alone.
brief.register: Vivid everyday description rather than an opaque whole idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 心跳快本身不分喜悅或害怕，也不證明將來表現如何；只描述人物當時感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要用情境分辨情緒，不由相同身體感受推相同原因。
brief.outcomeZh: 能配合具體情緒及時點描述心跳快。

listening.en: My heart was racing as I waited for my friend’s name to be announced for the award; I was excited for her, not worried about having to speak myself.
listening.zh: 等候宣布朋友獲獎名字時，我心跳很快；我是替她興奮，不是擔心自己要發言。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼心跳很快？

options.en: The speaker felt excited while waiting for a friend’s award announcement.
options.zh: 說話者等候朋友獲獎宣布，感到興奮。

options.en: The speaker was anxious about giving a personal acceptance speech.
options.zh: 說話者擔心自己要發表得獎感言。

options.en: The speaker felt calm because the award had already been announced.
options.zh: 獎項已宣布，所以說話者很平靜。

options.en: The speaker was disappointed after the friend’s name was left out.
options.zh: 朋友名字沒被選上後，說話者感到失望。

listening.explanationZh: excited for her 明確交代喜悅，not worried 排除自己發言的擔心；仍在等候宣布。

reply.promptEn: How did you feel while waiting to hear your friend’s name?
reply.promptZh: 等候聽到朋友名字時，你有甚麼感受？

options.en: I was thrilled for her and could feel my heartbeat speeding up.
options.zh: 我替她興奮，感到心跳加速。

options.en: My heart was racing with excitement.
options.zh: 我興奮得心跳很快。

options.en: The wait made me feel full of excited anticipation.
options.zh: 等候讓我滿懷興奮期待。

options.en: I felt a strong rush of excitement on her behalf.
options.zh: 我替她感到一陣強烈興奮。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述替朋友期待的興奮，不改成自己的發言恐懼。

scene.promptZh: 故事人物在漆黑走廊聽見陌生腳步，感到害怕，心跳加快；故事未交代最後找到誰。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her heart was racing as she waited to find out who was approaching.
options.zh: 等着弄清誰走近時，她心跳很快。

options.en: Her quick heartbeat shows she was delighted to see a friend she had already recognised.
options.zh: 心跳快顯示她已認出朋友，正高興相見。

options.en: She had already identified the footsteps and felt entirely at ease.
options.zh: 她已辨認腳步，感到完全安心。

scene.explanationZh: 害怕及尚未辨認的情境支援心跳快，卻沒有喜悅或已安心的結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜單憑 my heart was racing 得出？

options.en: The speaker noticed a rapid heartbeat.
options.zh: 說話者察覺心跳很快。

options.en: The surrounding story is needed to identify the emotion.
options.zh: 需看前後故事，才知是甚麼情緒。

options.en: The speaker must have been frightened rather than excited.
options.zh: 說話者一定是害怕，而不可能是興奮。

contrast.explanationZh: 相同快速心跳可出現在不同感受，需用語境判斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友聽你說頒獎時心跳很快，就以為你不想看朋友領獎；你當時其實很期待。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: My heart was racing because I was excited for her, not because I wanted to leave.
options.zh: 我心跳很快是替她興奮，不是想離開。

options.en: I was disappointed that the award was going to her rather than to me.
options.zh: 我失望的是獎項將給她，而不是給我。

options.en: My heartbeat sped up after she finished speaking, rather than while I waited for the announcement.
options.zh: 我在她講完後才心跳加快，而非等候宣布時。

dialogue.explanationZh: 最佳回應明說替她期待；失望及事後心跳都不符合已交代的感受與時點。

speaking.en: My heart was racing with excitement while I waited to hear whether our film had been selected.
speaking.zh: 等候知道短片是否獲選時，我興奮得心跳很快。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把情緒及等候時點說清楚。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為故事寫回顧旁白：人物去見多年未聯絡的哥哥，心跳很快；原以為只是高興，走到門前才發現也怕被問失聯原因。見面還未開始。用一至兩句第一人稱英文修正原先對感受的理解。

examples.en: My heart was racing, and I first called it excitement about seeing my brother. At his door, I realised I was also afraid of explaining why I had stayed away.
examples.zh: 我心跳很快，起初以為只是見哥哥的興奮。到他門前，我才發現也怕解釋為何一直沒來往。

examples.en: I thought my heart was racing only because I wanted to see him again, but that was not the whole feeling. Before I knocked, I noticed how nervous I was about the questions he might ask.
examples.zh: 我以為心跳快只因想再見他，但感受不止這樣。敲門前，我留意到自己多擔心他可能問的問題。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用走到門前才察覺的顧慮修正原有解釋，保留興奮與擔心可並存，不先編見面結果或只憑心跳診斷。

takeaways.en: Her heart was racing with nerves before the audition, even though she knew the piece well.
takeaways.zh: 試鏡前她緊張得心跳很快，儘管很熟悉樂段。

takeaways.en: My heart was racing when the curtain rose and I recognised my brother on stage.
takeaways.zh: 幕升起、我認出舞台上的哥哥時，心跳很快。

sources.sentence: After a few lessons, things began to click.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row9; unreported locators remain null.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: After several examples, the idea finally clicks.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page245, table2, row6; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Start to understand how an idea or process fits together.
brief.meaningZh: 開始理解一個想法或流程怎樣連起來。
brief.grammar: things began to click; the idea finally clicks; something clicked for me; informal intransitive click describes understanding, not pressing a mouse.
brief.register: Informal figurative click, supported by Cambridge become-clear sense.
brief.boundaryZh: 開始明白不等於所有步驟已精通；也不同於只背出一個正確答案而未理解。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可指出哪個關係變清楚，避免把成功猜中當已懂原理。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述理解出現的線索，並指出仍需練習的部分。

listening.en: When the tutor drew the route beside the timetable, things began to click: I could see why the later bus still arrived first, though I needed help reading the transfer symbols.
listening.zh: 導師把路線畫在時間表旁後，事情開始明白：我看出為何較後開的巴士反先到，但轉車符號仍需幫忙。
listening.promptZh: 說話者的理解有甚麼改變？

options.en: The route and timing started to make sense, while some symbols remained difficult.
options.zh: 路線與時間開始講得通，但部分符號仍有困難。

options.en: The speaker memorised a departure time without seeing why the arrival order differed.
options.zh: 說話者背下開車時間，仍不明白到站次序為何不同。

options.en: The transfer symbols were the only part understood; the arrival order remained unexplained.
options.zh: 只有轉車符號明白，到站次序仍沒解釋。

options.en: The speaker already understood every symbol before the tutor drew the route.
options.zh: 導師畫路線前，說話者已懂每個符號。

listening.explanationZh: could see why 是開始理解的證據；though 保留仍需協助的部分。

reply.promptEn: What changed when the tutor put the route beside the timetable?
reply.promptZh: 導師把路線放在時間表旁後，有甚麼改變？

options.en: Things began to click, especially the different arrival times.
options.zh: 事情開始明白，尤其是不同到站時間。

options.en: I saw how the route explained the arrival order.
options.zh: 我看出路線怎樣解釋到站次序。

options.en: The timing made more sense, even though the symbols still needed explanation.
options.zh: 時間較講得通，但符號仍需解釋。

options.en: I started connecting the journey information instead of reading isolated times.
options.zh: 我開始把旅程資料連起來，而非只讀分開的時間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述連結資料後的理解，保留未懂的符號。

scene.promptZh: 你學一個編織花樣，原只照動作，後來看見左右針怎樣形成斜紋，能解釋下一行應怎接，速度仍慢。哪句貼切？

options.en: Things are beginning to click, although I still work slowly.
options.zh: 事情開始明白，儘管我做得仍慢。

options.en: I can repeat the hand movements but cannot explain the pattern at all.
options.zh: 我只會重複手勢，完全不能解釋花樣。

options.en: I understood the pattern before seeing how the stitches connected.
options.zh: 看見針法怎連接前，我已懂這花樣。

scene.explanationZh: 看見連接及能解釋下一行是理解證據，不需先做得快。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 things began to click？

options.en: A learner explains why a new example follows the pattern.
options.zh: 學生解釋新例子為甚麼符合規律。

options.en: A learner copies a correct answer but still cannot explain any connection.
options.zh: 學生抄到正確答案，卻仍不能解釋任何關係。

options.en: A learner notices how two previously confusing steps fit together.
options.zh: 學生看出原本困惑的兩步怎樣連起來。

contrast.explanationZh: 抄對本身未顯示開始理解；要看關係是否變清楚。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說你仍需查轉車符號，所以剛才不算開始明白；你已能解釋到站次序。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Things began to click about the route, but I still need help with the symbols.
options.zh: 路線部分開始明白，但符號仍需幫忙。

options.en: Let us judge understanding only by whether I can name every symbol immediately.
options.zh: 只按我能否立即說出每個符號，判斷理解吧。

options.en: Because one detail is unclear, leave out the connection I can now explain.
options.zh: 一個細節不清楚，就不提我現在已能解釋的關係。

dialogue.explanationZh: 開始理解可以有範圍，與部分仍需協助並存。

speaking.en: Things began to click when I compared the two examples, but I still needed practice applying the rule.
speaking.zh: 比較兩個例子後，事情開始明白，但應用規則仍需練習。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明理解的線索及仍需練習之處。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你幫同伴核活動費用表，突然看出同一筆已付的運費重複輸入兩次，才令總額看似比單據多。你想解釋剛明白的關係，建議先與收據核對兩行、確認重複後更正；尚未核完其他數字。用一至兩句英文提議。

examples.en: Things began to click when I noticed the same delivery fee on two lines, although the receipt shows one payment. Could we check those entries against the receipt before correcting the total?
examples.zh: 我留意到同一筆運費列在兩行，收據卻顯示一筆付款後，事情開始明白。更正總額前，可否把那兩項與收據核對？

examples.en: The idea finally clicked when I saw that the delivery fee had been entered twice. Let us confirm the duplicate with the receipt and then check the other figures too.
examples.zh: 我看見運費被輸入兩次後，終於明白其中關係。我們先以收據確認重複，再核其他數字吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出同一筆運費兩次輸入與收據一筆付款的關係，先核再更正，不把發現一處當其餘數字已核完。

takeaways.en: The idea finally clicked when she explained why the two endings led to different reactions.
takeaways.zh: 她解釋兩個結尾為何引起不同反應後，那個想法終於明白了。

takeaways.en: Things began to click during the second demonstration, so I tried explaining the pattern in my own words.
takeaways.zh: 第二次示範時事情開始明白，所以我試用自己的話解釋規律。

sources.sentence: After the first paragraph, I began to get into the flow.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row10; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Begin working with a smooth, sustained rhythm and attention.
brief.meaningZh: 開始以順暢、持續而專注的節奏做事。
brief.grammar: get/got/getting into the flow of an activity; flow is an activity-rhythm metaphor here, not go with the flow meaning accept events without resisting.
brief.register: Natural figurative expression about a working rhythm; not claimed as a separately fixed dictionary idiom or clinical state.
brief.boundaryZh: 順暢專注不保證成品無誤，也不是隨別人決定；需交代活動怎由停頓變連貫。
brief.misconceptionZh: 先感到順手不等於不用檢查，也不代表任務已完成。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述進入做事節奏的過程，提出適合當下的安排。

listening.en: At first I stopped after every sentence of the letter, but once I had found the opening, I got into the flow and wrote for twenty minutes before checking the details.
listening.zh: 起初寫信每句都停，但找到開頭後，我進入順暢節奏，連寫二十分鐘才核細節。
listening.promptZh: 寫信的過程有甚麼轉變？

options.en: The speaker moved from repeated pauses to a sustained stretch of writing.
options.zh: 說話者由不斷停頓，轉成持續寫一段時間。

options.en: The speaker accepted someone else’s opinion instead of writing a personal letter.
options.zh: 說話者接受別人意見，不再寫自己的信。

options.en: Every sentence was checked before any further words could be written.
options.zh: 每句都先核完，才寫之後的字。

options.en: The speaker stopped as soon as the opening was found and left the rest for another day.
options.zh: 找到開頭便停，餘下留另一天寫。

listening.explanationZh: at first、once及twenty minutes比較停頓與連續寫作；核細節仍在之後。

reply.promptEn: Why did you leave the detail check until later in that writing session?
reply.promptZh: 那次寫信為甚麼較後才核細節？

options.en: I wanted to keep the sustained rhythm I had just found.
options.zh: 我想保持剛找到的持續節奏。

options.en: I had got into the flow and could keep the sentences moving.
options.zh: 我進入了順暢節奏，能繼續把句子寫下去。

options.en: I was making progress after a hesitant start.
options.zh: 猶豫的開頭之後，我正持續寫下去。

options.en: I chose to finish that stretch of drafting before reviewing details.
options.zh: 我選擇先完成那段初稿，再核細節。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋當次初稿與稍後核對的先後，不聲稱細節不重要。

scene.promptZh: 樂隊起初每幾小節便停，熟悉接段後終能連續演奏整段，之後仍需調整音量。哪句貼切？

options.en: We began to get into the flow once the transitions felt familiar.
options.zh: 接段較熟悉後，我們開始進入順暢節奏。

options.en: We decided to follow the loudest member’s choices without discussing the music.
options.zh: 我們不再討論音樂，決定一切跟最響亮的成員。

options.en: We were still stopping after every few bars, with no sustained passage yet.
options.zh: 我們仍每幾小節便停，尚無連續演奏段落。

scene.explanationZh: 連續演奏支持進入節奏，不是順從他人，也不排除音量仍需調整。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合此處 get into the flow？

options.en: 開始能連貫地投入一項活動。
把自己的判斷全交別人，不再主動參與。
原先常停頓，後來較能保持做事節奏。

contrast.explanationZh: 此處是自己投入活動的節奏，不是go with the flow的順應事情發展。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友見你順暢寫了一段，就說不用再核名字和日期；你仍計劃核細節。哪句回應較好？

options.en: I got into the flow while drafting, but I still need to check the names and dates.
options.zh: 初稿時我進入順暢節奏，但名字和日期仍需核對。

options.en: Keep all the details as they are, since smooth writing is enough evidence that they are accurate.
options.zh: 細節全照原樣吧，寫得順暢已足以證明正確。

options.en: Perhaps we should judge the names by how naturally they fit the sentences, rather than consult the original notes.
options.zh: 或許應按名字放在句子裏是否自然來判斷，而不用查原筆記。

dialogue.explanationZh: 初稿寫得連貫與資料準確不同；順口或自然的名字仍應查原資料，保留核對計劃最合適。

speaking.en: I got into the flow after the first few minutes, then set the draft aside for a careful check later.
speaking.zh: 起初幾分鐘後，我進入順暢節奏，之後把初稿放一旁，留待仔細核對。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清順暢投入與成品已正確。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：同伴準備剪接口述歷史錄音，剛開始做幾秒便被聊天訊息打斷。他想先試一小段不受打擾的工作時間，並約何時一起討論進度。用一至兩句英文向合作伙伴提出工作安排，不把安靜時間保證成剪接一定正確。

examples.en: Could we try fifteen minutes without messages so I can get into the flow of editing the recording? We can compare progress together at the end of that time.
examples.zh: 可否試十五分鐘不收訊息，讓我進入剪接錄音的順暢節奏？那段時間完後，我們可一起比較進度。

examples.en: I would like a short uninterrupted start to help me get into the flow. Shall we agree a time to discuss the edit instead of sending comments every few seconds?
examples.zh: 我想開始時有一小段不受打擾的時間，幫自己進入節奏。可否約時間談剪接，而非每幾秒傳意見？

glossary.zh: 一小段不受打擾的開始

writing.selfCheckZh: 開始前協商短時間試行及共同討論時點，不假定別人不能給意見，也不把順暢當正確保證。

takeaways.en: She got into the flow of the conversation once she stopped rehearsing every sentence in her head.
takeaways.zh: 不再在腦內預演每句後，她進入了順暢談話的節奏。

takeaways.en: We were getting into the flow, but we agreed to pause after the next section and review the plan.
takeaways.zh: 我們正進入順暢節奏，但同意下一段後停下檢視計劃。

Teach transparent working-rhythm use, not an asserted clinical flow diagnosis or universal productivity rule.

lessons.titleZh: 信心在嘗試之後逐漸建立

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: I learned that confidence comes after the first attempt.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row11; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Confidence may develop following an action or experience rather than being fully present beforehand.
brief.meaningZh: 信心可能在行動或經驗之後發展，不一定先完全具備。
brief.grammar: confidence comes/came/can come after + noun or -ing; after names sequence; a personal/general observation needs contextual qualification.
brief.register: Natural explanatory clause, not a fixed idiom or a universal psychological law.
brief.boundaryZh: after 指先後，不保證一次嘗試令人人有信心，也不表示不需準備或支援。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把某人的經驗改成所有人的必然規律；說清信心在哪方面增加。
brief.outcomeZh: 能連結具體嘗試與隨後感受，保留準備及個人差異。

listening.en: I expected to feel ready before reading aloud, but for me confidence came after the first supported attempt: the group waited patiently, and I found I could finish a short passage.
listening.zh: 我原以為朗讀前要先覺準備好，但對我而言，信心在首次有支援的嘗試後才來：小組耐心等，我發現能讀完一短段。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣描述信心與嘗試的先後？

options.en: A supported first reading helped the speaker feel more confident afterwards.
options.zh: 首次有支援的朗讀，幫說話者之後較有信心。

options.en: The speaker already felt fully confident before doing any reading.
options.zh: 尚未朗讀，說話者已完全有信心。

options.en: The speaker says preparation and other people’s patience were unnecessary.
options.zh: 說話者說準備和別人耐心都不需要。

options.en: The group’s first interruption prevented the speaker from completing the passage.
options.zh: 小組第一次打斷，令說話者沒能讀完段落。

listening.explanationZh: for me保留個人經驗；supported attempt、waited及finish支持嘗試後的信心。

reply.promptEn: Why did you not need to feel completely confident before joining the reading?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼不必先完全有信心才參與朗讀？

options.en: The patient group gave me room to try a short passage first.
options.zh: 耐心的小組給我空間，先試短段。

options.en: I discovered I could finish the passage with support.
options.zh: 我發現有支援便能讀完短段。

options.en: For me, confidence came after that first supported attempt.
options.zh: 對我而言，信心在首次有支援的嘗試之後才來。

options.en: Trying it showed me something that waiting alone had not.
options.zh: 試過讓我看見單是等待未能知道的事。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都連結已發生的支援嘗試，沒有保證其他人結果一樣。

scene.promptZh: 一位女學生照老師指導完成首次調色，也做出指定淡色，卻說仍不敢獨自再試，想多看一次示範。你只有這次已完成的觀察。哪句準確？

options.en: She finished the first attempt, but we cannot yet say that confidence came after it for her.
options.zh: 她完成了首次嘗試，但還不能說信心已隨之而來。

options.en: Completing the mix shows she already feels ready to work alone.
options.zh: 完成調色，顯示她已覺得可獨自做。

options.en: Her request for another demonstration means she did not complete the first mix.
options.zh: 她要求再看示範，表示首次調色沒完成。

scene.explanationZh: 完成動作與是否有信心不同；她明說仍不敢獨自試，不能由完成就代她斷定信心已增加。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論最不宜由 confidence comes after the first attempt 得出？

options.en: 信心可能不用在開始前就完全具備。
說話者下次換成較長篇章，也已不用原有支援。
需看嘗試的內容、支援及之後的感受。

contrast.explanationZh: 首次短段有支援的經驗，未證下次較長篇章已不需支援；需再看任務及本人感受。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把你的經驗寫成「所有新人都不需準備，做一次就有信心」；你當時有小組支援。哪句澄清較準確？

options.en: Confidence came after my first supported attempt, but that does not make preparation unnecessary for everyone.
options.zh: 我的信心在首次有支援的嘗試後才來，但不表示人人不需準備。

options.en: If the first reading helped, I can probably begin a much longer passage without the same support now.
options.zh: 既然首次朗讀有幫助，我現在大概可不用原支援便開始更長段落。

options.en: It sounds as though the confidence came from waiting to feel ready, rather than from the supported reading.
options.zh: 聽起來信心來自等到覺得準備好，而不是有支援的朗讀。

dialogue.explanationZh: 最佳回應保留本人嘗試後才增加信心及原有支援；未證較長任務可無支援，也沒有把信心放在嘗試之前。

speaking.en: For me, confidence came after a small first attempt with support, not before I had tried anything.
speaking.zh: 對我而言，信心在小小的首次有支援嘗試後才來，不是在尚未試過時。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再保留個人經驗、先後及支援。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你正為新會員寫歡迎訊息，自己曾在幾次有支援的帶路後才漸有信心。你想鼓勵他不必等完全有把握才開始，但不能保證他試一次就會有相同感受；可先談需要甚麼支援。用一至兩句英文直接寫給他。

examples.en: For me, confidence came after leading several walks with support, rather than before I started. You may feel differently, so shall we discuss what would help you try the first route?
examples.zh: 對我而言，信心在幾次有支援的帶路後才來，而非開始前。你的感受可能不同，可否先談甚麼會幫你試第一條路線？

examples.en: I found that confidence can come after trying, but I cannot promise how leading your first walk will feel. We can agree the support you want before you decide whether to lead a short section.
examples.zh: 我發現信心可能在嘗試後才來，但不能保證你首次帶路會有甚麼感受。你決定是否帶一小段前，我們可議你想要的支援。

glossary.zh: 在支援下帶領幾次步行

writing.selfCheckZh: 分清自己回顧所得與對新人的承諾，提供討論支援及選擇，而非要求他先有信心或保證首次必然增加。

takeaways.en: Her confidence came after she tried the introduction with a patient partner, rather than from waiting to feel certain.
takeaways.zh: 她跟耐心同伴試介紹之後才有信心，而非等到完全肯定才開始。

takeaways.en: For me, confidence came after the short rehearsal with my sister, though I still wanted to practise the longer speech.
takeaways.zh: 對我而言，跟姐姐短暫排練後才有信心，但我仍想練較長講稿。

review.author: AI root

english.evidence: Transparent confidence + come + after sequence construction. Source personal learned-that observation retained only as provenance; new attributed examples avoid universal psychological/causal promises.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese personally compared against each English subject, polarity, qualification and referent; no human approval claimed.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: You can move forward while your hands are still shaking.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page129, table1, row13; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: One’s hands continue to tremble; in this context the visible movement accompanies nervousness.
brief.meaningZh: 雙手仍持續顫抖；本課情境中，動作伴隨緊張。
brief.grammar: my/her hands are/were still shaking; still shows continuation; a literal bodily description whose emotional meaning comes from context.
brief.register: Vivid everyday description, not an opaque idiom or a medical diagnosis.
brief.boundaryZh: 手抖本身不證明失敗、不願意或完全不能行動；本課敘述需有緊張線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 感到緊張與仍願嘗試可以並存，不由動作推當事人已退出。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述仍在緊張的身體感受，提出有範圍的下一步。

listening.en: My hands were still shaking after I introduced the first guest, but I wanted to welcome the next one; I asked my partner to hold the cards while I spoke.
listening.zh: 介紹首位嘉賓後，我雙手仍發抖，但想繼續歡迎下一位；我請同伴在我說話時拿卡片。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣處理仍在緊張的情況？

options.en: The speaker continued with a specific piece of practical help.
options.zh: 說話者在一項具體幫助下繼續。

options.en: The speaker withdrew before introducing anyone.
options.zh: 說話者尚未介紹任何人便退出。

options.en: The shaking had stopped before the next welcome was discussed.
options.zh: 商量下一次歡迎前，手已停止發抖。

options.en: The partner took over every introduction while the speaker decided not to speak again.
options.zh: 同伴接手所有介紹，說話者決定不再發言。

listening.explanationZh: still保留感受持續；wanted及while I spoke顯示仍參與，卡片幫助不是全代替。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask your partner to hold the cards?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼請同伴拿卡片？

options.en: My hands were still shaking, but I wanted to continue speaking.
options.zh: 我雙手仍發抖，但想繼續說。

options.en: Holding the cards was difficult while I was nervous.
options.zh: 緊張時我較難拿穩卡片。

options.en: I wanted a small practical adjustment rather than to stop welcoming guests.
options.zh: 我想作一項小調整，而非停止歡迎嘉賓。

options.en: My partner could handle the cards while I gave the next introduction.
options.zh: 我作下一次介紹時，同伴可幫拿卡片。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應同一項實際支援，不把緊張改成已退出。

scene.promptZh: 一位女學生在社區會第一次提出意見後，雙手仍因緊張發抖，卻願留下回答一個簡單問題，請大家稍慢一點。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her hands are still shaking, but she is willing to answer the next question slowly.
options.zh: 她雙手仍發抖，但願慢慢答下一個問題。

options.en: Her visible nerves show that she has refused any further discussion.
options.zh: 看得見她緊張，就顯示她拒絕之後任何討論。

options.en: She has already finished answering every question and left the meeting.
options.zh: 她已答完每個問題，並離開會議。

scene.explanationZh: 願留下及請慢一點，說明緊張仍在卻繼續參與。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論最不宜由 her hands are still shaking 得出？

options.en: Her hands continue to tremble at this point.
options.zh: 在這個時點，她的手仍在顫抖。

options.en: She must already have decided to abandon the task.
options.zh: 她一定已決定放棄任務。

options.en: More context is needed to know how she feels and what she will do.
options.zh: 需更多情境，才知她感受及下一步。

contrast.explanationZh: 仍手抖描述動作，不直接確立放棄的決定。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴看到你手抖，便想直接替你說完；你願自己說，只想請他拿卡。哪句回應最合適？

options.en: My hands are still shaking, but I would like to speak; could you hold the cards for me?
options.zh: 我雙手仍發抖，但想自己說；可否幫我拿卡？

options.en: Could you read the introductions while I stay beside you and hold the cards?
options.zh: 可否由你讀介紹，我站在旁邊拿卡？

options.en: I would rather wait until my hands have stopped shaking before I try the next welcome.
options.zh: 我寧願等雙手停止發抖，才試下一次歡迎。

dialogue.explanationZh: 她想自己說，所需是別人拿卡；最佳回應說清兩點。代換角色或等到不抖才說，均不同於此刻願意繼續的要求。

speaking.en: My hands are still shaking, but I would like another moment and then I can try the introduction again.
speaking.zh: 我雙手仍發抖，但想再有片刻，之後可再試介紹。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清仍有緊張感與希望再試。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友邀你把剛完成的朗讀錄音發出去，你還在緊張，雙手仍發抖，想先自己重聽一遍，再決定是否分享；不是要朋友立即替你發佈。用一至兩句英文請他稍候。

examples.en: My hands are still shaking after the reading, so please give me a little time to listen back. I would like to decide about sharing it once I have heard the recording myself.
examples.zh: 朗讀後我雙手仍發抖，請給我一點時間重聽。我想親自聽過錄音後，才決定是否分享。

examples.en: I want to hear the recording before sending it out, even though my hands are still shaking. Could we wait until I have listened and said whether I am happy to share it?
examples.zh: 即使我雙手仍發抖，也想發出前先聽錄音。可否等我聽過、說明是否願意分享後才發？

writing.selfCheckZh: 坦白仍在緊張，提出重聽及自己決定的步驟，不把感受當已同意發佈或已放棄。

takeaways.en: Her hands were still shaking, but she asked to read the final sentence herself.
takeaways.zh: 她雙手仍發抖，但請求親自讀最後一句。

takeaways.en: My hands are still shaking after that first attempt; could we pause before deciding whether to record another?
takeaways.zh: 首次嘗試後我雙手仍發抖；可否先停一下，再決定是否錄另一段？

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Finishing the race showed I had broken a mental barrier.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page130, table1, row4; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: Overcome an internal fear or belief that had prevented an action.
brief.meaningZh: 克服原本妨礙行動的內心恐懼或想法。
brief.grammar: break/broke/have broken a mental barrier; identify the previously inhibiting belief and what the person managed to attempt.
brief.register: Transparent barrier metaphor; not a clinical treatment claim.
brief.boundaryZh: 克服一個內心限制，不代表相關任務都已掌握或日後不再緊張；需有前後的具體差別。
brief.misconceptionZh: 原本害怕而不敢做，與只是缺乏器材或時間不同；說清是哪一種阻礙。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體經歷表達跨過心理限制，保留仍需學習的部分。

listening.en: I had avoided asking questions in the group because I feared sounding foolish; asking one and receiving a thoughtful reply showed me I had broken a mental barrier, though I still prepared my words carefully.
listening.zh: 我怕顯得愚笨，一直不敢在小組問問題；問一次並獲認真回覆，讓我覺得跨過心中障礙，但仍會仔細準備用詞。
listening.promptZh: 說話者所說的障礙是甚麼？

options.en: A fear of appearing foolish had kept the speaker from asking.
options.zh: 怕顯得愚笨，原本令說話者不敢問。

options.en: A lack of available meeting rooms had prevented questions.
options.zh: 沒有可用會議室，原本阻止大家問問題。

options.en: The speaker had already mastered every topic before asking.
options.zh: 提問前，說話者已掌握每個主題。

options.en: The group had refused to allow any questions even after this reply.
options.zh: 即使已回覆，小組仍拒絕容許任何提問。

listening.explanationZh: feared sounding foolish是內心限制，實際提問跨過它；仍準備字句不否定改變。

reply.promptEn: Why did asking that one question matter to you?
reply.promptZh: 問那一個問題為甚麼對你重要？

options.en: It helped me act despite a fear that had kept me silent.
options.zh: 它幫我在原本令我沉默的恐懼下行動。

options.en: I had broken a mental barrier by trying something I had avoided.
options.zh: 我嘗試原本逃避的事，跨過心中障礙。

options.en: The thoughtful reply changed my expectation of being judged foolish.
options.zh: 認真回覆改變了我對被視為愚笨的預期。

options.en: I could see that asking was possible, even though I still needed preparation.
options.zh: 我看見可以開口問，儘管仍需準備。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明原本恐懼與實際行動的改變，不聲稱已懂所有主題。

scene.promptZh: 一位女畫者早已願意公開素描，卻因展廳沒有空位而未能展出；後來主辦者騰出牆面，她便交作品。哪句最準確？

options.en: Space became available; this account does not show her breaking a mental barrier.
options.zh: 有空間可用了；這敘述沒有顯示她跨過內心障礙。

options.en: Finding a wall shows that she has overcome a fear of people seeing her drawings.
options.zh: 找到牆面，顯示她已克服讓人看畫的恐懼。

options.en: She had a place to exhibit from the start but was unwilling to submit a sketch.
options.zh: 她起初已有展出位置，卻不願交素描。

scene.explanationZh: 她原本已願意公開，改變的是可用空間；沒有內心限制前後改變的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 broken a mental barrier 的此處用法？

options.en: A person attempts something previously avoided through fear of judgement.
options.zh: 一個人嘗試原本怕被評價而逃避的事。

options.en: A delivery of missing paper lets an already willing artist begin working.
options.zh: 補送缺少的紙，讓本來就願意作畫的人開始。

options.en: A person revises an internal belief after an experience shows action is possible.
options.zh: 經歷顯示可行動後，一個人改變原有內心想法。

contrast.explanationZh: 本來願意卻缺紙是實際資源問題，未交代跨過內心限制。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你仍準備問句，就代表沒跨過障礙；你以前連問也不敢，現在已試過。哪句回應最準確？

options.en: I have broken a mental barrier about speaking up, but preparing a question still helps me.
options.zh: 我已跨過開口的心中障礙，但準備問題仍有幫助。

options.en: I should wait to ask again until I no longer need written notes.
options.zh: 我應等到不再需要書面筆記，才再次提問。

options.en: Perhaps the useful reply, rather than my willingness to ask, is the change the phrase describes.
options.zh: 或許這表達說的改變是回覆有用，而非我願意提問。

dialogue.explanationZh: 跨過的是原本不敢開口的限制；準備筆記不取消此改變，別人的回覆有用也不是障礙本身。

speaking.en: I had broken a mental barrier by sharing the sketch, although I still had plenty to learn about drawing.
speaking.zh: 分享素描讓我跨過心中障礙，但繪畫仍有很多要學。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清內心限制與仍需培養的能力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你先前已克服害怕被評價、敢在讀書會提問。朋友現在邀你即場解釋一本你未讀的新書，以為你既已跨過障礙便能應付；你想肯定自己的改變，卻婉拒假裝熟悉，改提先閱讀再討論。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I have broken a mental barrier about asking questions, but that does not mean I know the book you have chosen. Could I read it first and join the discussion next week?
examples.zh: 我已跨過提問的心中障礙，但不表示熟悉你選的書。可否讓我先讀，下周再參與討論？

examples.en: Breaking a mental barrier helped me speak up; it did not give me knowledge of an unread book. I would rather prepare before offering an explanation.
examples.zh: 跨過心中障礙幫我開口，卻沒有令我懂一本未讀的書。我寧願先準備，再作解釋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把已跨過的內心限制與未有的書本知識分開，有禮提出先閱讀，不抹去進步或假裝熟悉。

takeaways.en: She broke a mental barrier when she let the group hear a song she had kept private for years.
takeaways.zh: 讓小組聽多年一直保密的歌時，她跨過心中障礙。

takeaways.en: He had broken a mental barrier about asking for help, but he still chose carefully whom to approach.
takeaways.zh: 他跨過了求助的心中障礙，但仍仔細選向誰開口。

brief.meaningEn: An emotional inhibition or sense of separation eases, allowing more open interaction.
brief.meaningZh: 內心的拘謹或隔閡減退，讓人較能坦誠交流。
brief.grammar: the wall came down between us/once...; wall is a contextual emotional metaphor, not a physical structure in this lesson.
brief.register: Creative but readily understandable emotional-wall metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 隔閡減退不等於所有人已完全互信或今後沒有保留；需指出交流有何具體轉變。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因大家待在同一房間便說心中隔閡消退，要有願交流的線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述由拘謹到較願分享的轉變，保留合適的私人界限。

listening.en: I had stayed quiet in the new group, but when I mentioned my grandmother’s songs, the wall came down: others shared their own memories, and I stopped rehearsing every reply in my head.
listening.zh: 在新小組我一直少說話，但提起祖母的歌後，隔閡消退：別人分享自己的回憶，我也不再在腦內預演每句回覆。
listening.promptZh: 這裏的 wall came down 描述甚麼改變？

options.en: The conversation became more open after a shared personal topic.
options.zh: 有了共同個人話題後，談話變得較開放。

options.en: The group had only changed the seating, while everyone remained silent.
options.zh: 小組只改了座位，大家仍沉默。

options.en: The speaker decided to keep every memory private and leave.
options.zh: 說話者決定所有回憶保密，並離開。

options.en: Others repeated a prepared introduction without responding to the songs.
options.zh: 別人只重複準備好的介紹，沒有回應歌曲。

listening.explanationZh: 分享回憶及不用預演回覆，具體支持拘謹減退；不是只換地方或關閉交流。

reply.promptEn: Why did you feel more at ease in the new group?
reply.promptZh: 在新小組為甚麼後來較自在？

options.en: The wall came down when our memories gave us something real to share.
options.zh: 回憶讓大家有真實內容分享時，隔閡消退了。

options.en: People responded with their own stories instead of leaving me to perform an introduction.
options.zh: 大家以自己的故事回應，而非只讓我表演介紹。

options.en: I began answering naturally rather than planning each reply in advance.
options.zh: 我開始自然回應，而非先計劃每句。

options.en: The familiar songs opened a warmer exchange between us.
options.zh: 熟悉的歌讓我們有較親切的交流。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據實際分享回憶及回應，沒有誇大成所有私事已公開。

scene.promptZh: 兩位同伴由長桌兩端改坐相鄰，卻仍只回覆工作清單，不願談自己對合作的感受。你想避免把座位變近當情緒已較開放。哪句準確？

options.en: They are sitting closer, but there is not yet evidence that the wall has come down.
options.zh: 他們坐近了，但尚無證據顯示情緒隔閡已消退。

options.en: The wall came down as soon as they changed seats, before either said anything more.
options.zh: 一換座位隔閡就消退，不用任何人多說甚麼。

options.en: Their replies show that they have begun discussing the personal meaning of the project.
options.zh: 他們的回覆顯示已開始談項目對自己的個人意義。

scene.explanationZh: 實際距離變近，交流內容卻仍拘謹；需有較開放的回應線索才支持情緒隔閡減退。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持此處 the wall came down？

options.en: People begin responding openly after a previously guarded exchange.
options.zh: 原本拘謹的交流後，大家開始較坦誠回應。

options.en: People sit closer but continue to avoid speaking to each other.
options.zh: 大家坐得較近，卻仍避開互相說話。

options.en: A person becomes less self-conscious and shares a meaningful memory.
options.zh: 一個人較不拘謹，分享有意義的回憶。

contrast.explanationZh: 物理距離改變未必帶來情緒隔閡的改變，要有交流線索。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說隔閡消退，就可替全組分享所有家事；你只看見大家較願談歌和回憶。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: The wall came down in that conversation, but we should still ask before sharing anyone’s private story.
options.zh: 那次談話中隔閡消退，但分享別人的私事前仍應先問。

options.en: She told the group the story, so I already have permission to include it in the public introduction.
options.zh: 她已向小組說故事，所以我已獲許可把它放公開介紹。

options.en: Perhaps we should describe only the song choice and say nothing about the change in how people responded.
options.zh: 或許只描述選了哪首歌，不提大家回應方式的改變。

dialogue.explanationZh: 小組分享不等於公開許可；最佳回應保留實際交流變化，並在分享故事前先問本人。

speaking.en: The wall came down once we started sharing our memories, though we still respected what each person wanted to keep private.
speaking.zh: 開始分享回憶後，隔閡消退了，但我們仍尊重每人想保密的內容。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述交流變得較開放及仍有界限。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你設計小說兩人重逢的一幕，起初只客氣談天氣，後來一人承認仍留着對方送的書，另一人才願問起當年誤會。你想向編輯建議先用這小物件打開談話，再慢慢談分歧，不立即寫成一切已和好。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: I would let the wall come down when she admits she kept his book, so they can begin an honest conversation. The old disagreement can remain unresolved while they start listening.
examples.zh: 我會讓她承認留着他的書時，隔閡消退，好讓坦誠談話開始。舊分歧可仍未解，但他們開始聆聽。

examples.en: The wall comes down over the old book before either character knows how to settle the misunderstanding. I would show a first sincere question rather than an instant reconciliation.
examples.zh: 兩人尚不知如何解決誤會，隔閡已因舊書而消退。我會寫首個真誠問題，而非立即和好。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用保留舊書及開始真誠提問呈現隔閡減退，保留分歧仍待談，不把開口當全部和好。

takeaways.en: The wall came down when he admitted he had also found the first meeting awkward.
takeaways.zh: 他承認也覺得初次見面尷尬後，隔閡消退了。

takeaways.en: That wall has come down enough for us to discuss the difficult memory, although we still take it slowly.
takeaways.zh: 隔閡已減退，讓我們能談那段難受回憶，但仍慢慢來。

brief.meaningEn: Depend on a person or resource for help; too heavily adds a judgement that the reliance is excessive.
brief.meaningZh: 依靠某人或資源獲得幫助；too heavily 另加依賴過多的評價。
brief.grammar: lean/leaned/leant/leaning on someone/something; lean on it too heavily; support sense, distinct from lean on someone to do something meaning pressure them.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb; context distinguishes supportive reliance from coercive pressure.
brief.boundaryZh: 依靠不一定是壞事；too heavily 才說過多，需指出有甚麼能力或責任被取代。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把正常求助一概當過度依賴，也不能只因工具省時就忽略自己未做的核對。
brief.outcomeZh: 能肯定適當支援，同時具體說明依賴過多的限制。

listening.en: The checklist helped at first, but I leaned on it too heavily and stopped noticing requests that were not listed; now I use it as a reminder and ask about anything unusual.
listening.zh: 起初清單有幫助，但我過度依賴它，不再留意表上沒有的要求；現在我用它提醒，遇特別情況便詢問。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣評價清單的用途？

options.en: It was useful support, but relying on it alone made unusual requests easier to miss.
options.zh: 清單是有用支援，但只靠它令特別要求較易被漏看。

options.en: The speaker abandoned the checklist and now works from memory alone.
options.zh: 說話者已放棄清單，現在只憑記憶做事。

options.en: The speaker now uses the checklist to avoid asking about unusual cases.
options.zh: 說話者現用清單，避免詢問特別個案。

options.en: The difficulty was caused by checking too many unusual requests with other people.
options.zh: 困難是因向別人核問太多特別要求而起。

listening.explanationZh: 清單原有幫助，過度只靠它才漏看表外要求；現仍用作提醒並詢問，並非放棄或問得太多。

reply.promptEn: Why have you changed how you use the checklist?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼改變使用清單的方法？

options.en: I was treating the list as if it covered unusual requests too.
options.zh: 我原把清單當作連特別要求也全涵蓋。

options.en: I leaned on it too heavily instead of noticing what was missing.
options.zh: 我過度依賴它，沒留意缺少甚麼。

options.en: It helped with routine reminders, but I needed to ask about exceptions.
options.zh: 它有助日常提醒，但例外需詢問。

options.en: I wanted to keep its useful prompts without replacing my attention to new information.
options.zh: 我想保留有用提示，而不讓它取代對新資料的留意。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均交代過度依賴的具體代價及仍可保留的支援。

scene.promptZh: 女同事到陌生工場，先依靠熟悉流程的同伴解釋規則，自己也記筆記和查不明處；沒有把所有責任交人。哪句貼切？

options.en: She can lean on her colleague for guidance while learning the process herself.
options.zh: 她可依靠同事指引，同時自己學流程。

options.en: She is relying on her colleague to make the notes and handle the unclear cases for her.
options.zh: 她依靠同事替她記筆記及處理不明個案。

options.en: The colleague’s explanation means she no longer needs to notice unfamiliar cases.
options.zh: 同伴解釋過，就表示她不需再留意陌生情況。

scene.explanationZh: 同事提供指引，她仍自己記錄及核問；求助不等於已把記錄與處理責任交人。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合此處 lean on？

options.en: A person may use reliable help while retaining responsibility.
options.zh: 一個人可用可靠支援，同時保留責任。

options.en: Every instance of leaning on support must be excessive.
options.zh: 每次依靠支援都一定過度。

options.en: Too heavily adds a warning about the amount or role of reliance.
options.zh: Too heavily對依靠程度或作用加上警告。

contrast.explanationZh: 依靠本身不貶義，過多需由程度及後果說明；另有施壓意思需看不同情境。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友聽你說原本過度依賴清單，就要把清單全刪；它仍能提醒一般步驟。哪句回應最合適？

options.en: I should not lean on it too heavily, but I can keep it for reminders and ask about unusual cases.
options.zh: 我不應過度依賴它，但可保留作提醒，特別情況再問。

options.en: Adding more examples to the list should be enough; I can keep looking only for the requests it names.
options.zh: 在清單加例子便應足夠；我可繼續只留意表上寫的要求。

options.en: Perhaps I should put the list aside and use memory for the usual steps too.
options.zh: 或許應收起清單，一般步驟也只憑記憶。

dialogue.explanationZh: 延長清單未處理忽略表外要求的習慣，全棄也失去提醒作用；保留提醒並核問特例才合適。

speaking.en: I can lean on my friend for advice while making the final choice myself.
speaking.zh: 我可依靠朋友的意見，同時自己作最後選擇。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清適當求助與把責任全交別人。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要第一次主持街坊討論，想請熟悉居民的朋友事前提醒需要留意的語氣；你會自己準備議程和主持，不期待他代答每個問題。用一至兩句英文請求合適支援。

examples.en: Could I lean on you for advice about the tone before the discussion? I will prepare the agenda and lead it myself, but your knowledge of the residents would help.
examples.zh: 討論前可否依靠你的意見，提醒我語氣？我會自己準備議程和主持，但你對居民的認識會有幫助。

examples.en: Could I lean on you for guidance about wording if I send you the agenda first? I will prepare and host the discussion myself, but would value your advice on the residents’ concerns.
examples.zh: 我先傳議程給你，可否依靠你指引哪些用詞需留意？我會自己準備及主持討論，但珍惜你對居民顧慮的意見。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出範圍清楚的語氣意見請求，保留自己主持及準備責任；不把求助當命令朋友或過度依賴。

takeaways.en: She leaned on her brother for encouragement while choosing which course to try.
takeaways.zh: 選擇試哪個課程時，她依靠哥哥的鼓勵。

takeaways.en: I leaned on the guide too heavily and missed the change announced at the entrance.
takeaways.zh: 我過度依賴指南，漏看入口剛宣布的改動。

sources.sentence: The discussion was hard because two truths rub against each other.

brief.meaningEn: Two valid observations or concerns create tension when considered together.
brief.meaningZh: 兩項都成立的觀察或考慮，放在一起便產生張力。
brief.grammar: two truths rub against each other; an explicit creative friction metaphor; explain both truths rather than present a formal logical contradiction.
brief.register: Reflective figurative wording, not a fixed dictionary idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 兩項都成立而有取捨，不表示其中一項必是假，也不表示可省去比較。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要交代兩項考慮及如何衝突，不把普通意見不同自動說成兩項真理。
brief.outcomeZh: 能承認相互牽制的實際考慮，提出保留兩者的討論方法。

listening.en: Here, two truths rub against each other: pupils need quiet time to finish a difficult piece, and they also need chances to ask one another for help; our plan has to make room for both.
listening.zh: 這裏兩項真實考慮互相牽制：學生需安靜時間完成難題，也需互相求助的機會；計劃要兼顧兩者。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看待安靜與求助？

options.en: Both needs matter, but arranging them together creates a practical tension.
options.zh: 兩項需要都重要，但一起安排有實際張力。

options.en: The need to ask for help has been disproved by the need for quiet.
options.zh: 需要安靜，已證明求助需要不成立。

options.en: The speaker wants pupils to stop asking anyone for help.
options.zh: 說話者想學生停止向任何人求助。

options.en: The two needs are described as identical, so no scheduling choice is needed.
options.zh: 兩項需要被說成完全相同，不需安排取捨。

listening.explanationZh: need及also need肯定兩者，make room for both要求兼顧，未否定其一或說沒有張力。

reply.promptEn: Why can you not solve the classroom plan simply by insisting on silence?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼不能只要求安靜就解決課堂安排？

options.en: Pupils need opportunities to ask for help as well as time to concentrate.
options.zh: 學生既需專注時間，也需求助機會。

options.en: The plan has to respect two real needs that can compete for the same time.
options.zh: 計劃要尊重兩項可能爭同一時段的實際需要。

options.en: Two truths rub against each other: pupils need quiet concentration, but they also need to ask for help.
options.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制：學生需安靜專注，也需求助。

options.en: Complete silence alone would leave the need for discussion unaddressed.
options.zh: 單是完全安靜，仍未處理討論的需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都肯定兩項需要，不把一項當唯一標準。

scene.promptZh: 小劇場需要票款維持開門，也想讓收入較少的居民能進場；討論的是怎樣安排部分低價場，不是否定收入需要。哪句貼切？

options.en: Two truths rub against each other: the theatre needs income, and access matters too.
options.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制：劇場需收入，入場機會也重要。

options.en: Concern about access shows that the theatre has no running costs.
options.zh: 重視入場機會，顯示劇場沒有營運成本。

options.en: The need for income means the residents’ access is not a real concern.
options.zh: 需要收入，就表示居民入場機會並非真正考慮。

scene.explanationZh: 成本與入場機會都成立，需找安排，不能用一項否定另一項。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 two truths rub against each other？

options.en: Both observations can be valid while creating a difficult choice.
options.zh: 兩項觀察都可成立，同時令選擇困難。

options.en: One statement must be false merely because the needs are difficult to combine.
options.zh: 只因兩項需要難兼顧，就必有一句是假。

options.en: The speaker should explain the tension rather than just repeat the metaphor.
options.zh: 說話者應解釋張力，而不只重複比喻。

contrast.explanationZh: 實際需要有取捨，不等於形式邏輯上只能一句成立。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說既然要兼顧就無法決定，應隨便選；你仍想比較不同安排。哪句回應較好？

options.en: Two truths rub against each other, but we can compare plans by how well each protects both needs.
options.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制，但可比較各方案怎樣保留兩項需要。

options.en: Leave out the discussion need so the plan looks simpler on paper.
options.zh: 不提討論需要，讓紙上的計劃較簡單。

options.en: Treat the tension as proof that no reason could make one arrangement better.
options.zh: 把張力當成沒有理由能令某方案較好的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認張力仍可按兩項需要比較，不必刪除一項或放棄判斷。

speaking.en: Two truths rub against each other: we need time to work alone, and we also learn by discussing our questions.
speaking.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制：我們需獨立做事的時間，也透過討論問題學習。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再清楚說出兩項成立而需兼顧的考慮。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們想整理家族回憶，長輩既珍惜把故事留給後人，也想有些敏感片段只留家人聽。你想在群組提議先標哪些可公開、哪些需保密，承認兩項考慮都重要，不替大家擅自公開。用一至兩句英文建議。

examples.en: Two truths rub against each other: we want to preserve the stories, and some memories need privacy. Could we mark what can be shared before preparing a public version?
examples.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制：我們想保留故事，有些回憶也需私隱。準備公開版前，可否先標哪些可分享？

examples.en: Two truths rub against each other when preserving family history also involves private experiences. Let us ask which passages can be public and keep the others within the family.
examples.zh: 保留家史同時涉及私人經歷時，兩項真實考慮互相牽制。一起問哪些片段可公開，其餘留在家人內。

writing.selfCheckZh: 同時肯定保存與私隱，用先問及標示範圍作安排，不把其一當假或替所有人給許可。

takeaways.en: Two truths rub against each other: the archive needs protection, and people need ways to learn from it.
takeaways.zh: 兩項真實考慮互相牽制：檔案需保護，人們也需有方法從中學習。

takeaways.en: Two truths rub against each other in the rehearsal plan: the group needs time together, but some members can only attend after work.
takeaways.zh: 排練計劃中，兩項真實考慮互相牽制：小組需一起練的時間，但有些成員下班後才能到。

brief.meaningEn: A simple, tidy response that appears to settle a question without loose ends.
brief.meaningZh: 看似簡潔俐落、能把問題交代妥當的答案。
brief.grammar: a neat answer to a question; no neat answer; neat describes tidy simplicity, not handwriting in this use.
brief.register: Natural evaluative collocation, often negated when a problem has competing considerations.
brief.boundaryZh: no neat answer 不表示沒有任何可行做法，也不代表不用證據；簡潔答案仍要能回應情境。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分清答案簡潔與答案充分，不把短或好看當自動正確。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出問題為何難用簡單答案概括，仍提出具體下一步。

listening.en: There was no neat answer to where the club should meet: the quiet room had few seats, while the larger room was often noisy, so we asked members which problem mattered most for each activity.
listening.zh: 社團在哪裏聚會沒有簡單俐落答案：安靜房座位少，大房又常吵，所以我們問成員各活動最在意哪項問題。
listening.promptZh: 沒有 neat answer 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The rooms involve different drawbacks that need to be weighed for the activity.
options.zh: 兩個房間有不同缺點，需按活動衡量。

options.en: The speaker is mainly concerned that the written answer looks untidy.
options.zh: 說話者主要嫌書面答案字跡不整齊。

options.en: The quiet room had enough seats, but the members rejected it because it was too far away.
options.zh: 安靜房座位足夠，但成員嫌太遠而拒絕。

options.en: The larger room solved the seating problem, and noise was not part of the comparison.
options.zh: 大房解決座位問題，噪音不在比較之列。

listening.explanationZh: 安靜房座位少，大房常吵，兩項限制需按活動衡量；並未說距離才是問題，或比較時無需顧噪音。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask members about the rooms instead of choosing immediately?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼先問成員對房間的看法，而非立即選？

options.en: There was no neat answer because quietness and capacity pointed to different rooms.
options.zh: 安靜與容納人數指向不同房間，沒有簡單俐落答案。

options.en: I needed to know which drawback mattered for the activity.
options.zh: 我需知道活動較在意哪個缺點。

options.en: Each option solved one problem while creating another.
options.zh: 每個選項解決一項問題，也帶來另一項。

options.en: A quick choice would have hidden a trade-off the members should discuss.
options.zh: 太快選會掩蓋成員應討論的取捨。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明取捨及諮詢，不表示沒有辦法或無需判斷。

scene.promptZh: 學生想用一句口號解釋一個人物為何離家，但故事同時寫工作機會、家人期望及個人想法，單一原因會漏線索。哪句貼切？

options.en: There is no neat answer that reduces her choice to only one cause.
options.zh: 沒有簡單俐落答案能把她的選擇只歸一個原因。

options.en: The job offer is the main explanation, so the family passages can be treated as background without examining them.
options.zh: 工作邀請是主要解釋，所以家人段落可只當背景，不用細看。

options.en: The character’s private wishes should be treated separately, without asking how they connect to the job and family expectations.
options.zh: 應把人物自己的想法另看，不問它與工作及家人期望怎相連。

scene.explanationZh: 故事同時給多項線索，需看如何相連；先只重工作或把個人想法孤立，都漏了題目要求。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解最不符合 no neat answer？

options.en: A simple response may leave important considerations unresolved.
options.zh: 簡單回應可能仍留重要考慮未處理。

options.en: Careful comparison may still support a workable next step.
options.zh: 仔細比較仍可支持可行的下一步。

options.en: No relevant evidence can help us choose any action.
options.zh: 任何相關證據都不能幫我們選行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有簡單概括，不等於沒有判斷或行動依據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴因房間選擇沒有簡單答案，就想取消整個社團；你已有兩個能按活動比較的選項。哪句回應較好？

options.en: There is no neat answer, but we can ask which room suits each activity instead of abandoning the club.
options.zh: 沒有簡單俐落答案，但可問各活動適合哪個房，而非放棄社團。

options.en: Let us choose the larger room now; enough seats should settle which space suits the club.
options.zh: 現在選大房吧；座位夠，就應能決定哪個空間適合社團。

options.en: The quiet room seems best to me, so we can book it before asking how many people each activity brings.
options.zh: 我看安靜房最好，可先訂，之後才問各活動多少人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按活動問清安靜及人數需要，才可比較；只看座位或先訂安靜房，都過早以一項優點定案。

speaking.en: There is no neat answer to this question, but comparing the evidence can still help us choose a sensible next step.
speaking.zh: 這問題沒有簡單俐落答案，但比較證據仍可幫我們選合理下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把沒有簡單答案與沒有任何方法分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友要把自己照顧舊花園的經歷寫成「只要努力就一定成功」，但有些植物靠鄰居提醒、有些仍種不活。你想建議文章保留不整齊的真實細節，寫出努力、幫助與限制，不只留口號。用一至兩句英文給編輯意見。

examples.en: There is no neat answer that makes effort explain everything in your garden story. I would keep the neighbour’s help and the plants that did not survive, so readers can see what really happened.
examples.zh: 花園故事沒有簡單俐落答案，能用努力解釋一切。我會保留鄰居幫助及沒種活的植物，讓讀者看到實況。

examples.en: A neat answer about effort alone would leave out the help and uncertainty in the garden. Could you include those details instead of ending with a promise that hard work always succeeds?
examples.zh: 只談努力的簡潔答案會漏掉花園裏的幫助及不確定。可否保留細節，而非以努力必成功的保證作結？

writing.selfCheckZh: 以實際細節說明口號不足，提出保留內容的修改，不把複雜當沒經驗可寫。

takeaways.en: The writer resisted a neat answer because the letters revealed several different reasons for the move.
takeaways.zh: 信件顯示搬遷有幾個不同原因，所以作者不願給簡單概括。

takeaways.en: There was no neat answer about the rooms, so we compared the quiet smaller space with the noisier hall before choosing.
takeaways.zh: 房間選擇沒有簡單俐落答案，所以我們先比較安靜小房及較吵禮堂，才作決定。

brief.meaningEn: A better-defined principle or sense of direction for deciding what to do.
brief.meaningZh: 較明確的原則或方向，幫助決定下一步。
brief.grammar: give/provide someone with a clearer compass for decisions; compass is an extended guidance metaphor; clearer compares the guidance with before.
brief.register: Reflective creative noun metaphor, related to a compass not a cage but without that guidance-versus-restriction contrast.
brief.boundaryZh: 方向較明確不等於每步已有答案或保證成功；需說明準則怎幫選擇。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只用漂亮比喻，要交代哪個原則變清楚及還需決定甚麼。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體準則表達較清晰的方向，保留實際選擇。

listening.en: Agreeing that every visitor should understand the first instruction gave us a clearer compass for the redesign: we could compare signs by that aim, even though we still had several layouts to test.
listening.zh: 同意每位訪客應看懂首個指示，讓重新設計有較清楚方向：可按這目標比較標牌，但仍有幾種版面要測試。
listening.promptZh: 討論帶來甚麼幫助？

options.en: It established a clearer criterion for comparing designs without settling every layout.
options.zh: 它建立較清楚的比較準則，但沒決定每個版面。

options.en: It chose one final layout before any testing was needed.
options.zh: 它在不需任何測試前，已選定最後版面。

options.en: It replaced the visitors’ understanding with the designers’ favourite colours as the main aim.
options.zh: 它把主要目標由訪客理解改成設計者喜歡的顏色。

options.en: The group now had no reason to compare the remaining layouts.
options.zh: 小組現已沒有理由比較餘下版面。

listening.explanationZh: compare by that aim指導選擇，still layouts to test保留未完成的判斷。

reply.promptEn: What did agreeing the main aim change for your redesign?
reply.promptZh: 同意主要目標，對重新設計有甚麼改變？

options.en: We gained a clearer compass for judging the signs.
options.zh: 我們判斷標牌有了較清楚方向。

options.en: We could ask whether each layout helped a visitor understand the first instruction.
options.zh: 我們可問每種版面是否幫訪客看懂首個指示。

options.en: The discussion gave us a shared criterion for the next tests.
options.zh: 討論給下次測試一項共同準則。

options.en: We had a firmer sense of what the design was meant to achieve.
options.zh: 我們較清楚設計要達到甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述準則與目標，而不把方向當版面已定。

scene.promptZh: 學生原不知怎選訪問材料，後來同意只保留直接幫讀者理解人物選擇的片段；仍需逐段查。哪句貼切？

options.en: That principle gives us a clearer compass for selecting the interview passages.
options.zh: 這原則為選訪問片段提供較清楚方向。

options.en: The new principle makes relevance less important than keeping the interviews evenly represented.
options.zh: 新原則令相關性不如平均保留各訪問重要。

options.en: We should now keep whichever passage is longest, regardless of its relevance.
options.zh: 現應保留最長的片段，不管是否相關。

scene.explanationZh: 準則是幫讀者理解人物選擇，仍需逐段看相關性；不是改成平均份量或最長片段。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a clearer compass 的這種比喻得出？

options.en: The person has a better-defined basis for making choices.
options.zh: 當事人有較明確的選擇依據。

options.en: Every practical decision has already been made correctly.
options.zh: 每個實際決定都已正確作好。

options.en: The context should say which guiding principle became clearer.
options.zh: 情境應交代哪個指導原則較清楚。

contrast.explanationZh: 指南針比喻方向，不保證每步已選妥或正確。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說既然目標清楚，就不用再試標牌；你們仍有不同版面。哪句回應較好？

options.en: We have a clearer compass, but we still need to test which layout serves that aim best.
options.zh: 我們方向較清楚，但仍需測試哪種版面最配合目標。

options.en: Since we agree on the aim, the layout we already prefer should be the first choice without a visitor trial.
options.zh: 既然同意目標，原本最喜歡的版面就應不用訪客試看而優先選。

options.en: During the trial, let us rank the layouts by colour appeal rather than whether visitors understand the first instruction.
options.zh: 試看時，一起按顏色吸引力排名，而非訪客是否看懂首個指示。

dialogue.explanationZh: 共同目標是測試準則，不是偏好版面的證據；測試時也不能換成顏色吸引力。

speaking.en: The discussion gave us a clearer compass for our choices, though we still had to compare the practical options.
speaking.zh: 討論給選擇較清楚方向，但仍需比較實際方案。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明指引怎幫選擇而非代作每步。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想加入更多活動，卻發現自己最重視每周能專心照顧祖母的一晚。說清這優先次序後，一個有趣但與那晚衝突的新邀請來了；你想有禮婉拒並解釋決定，不替其他人定同一優先。用一至兩句英文回覆邀請者。

examples.en: Knowing which evening I want to keep for my grandmother has given me a clearer compass for new commitments. Thank you for inviting me, but I will keep that evening free rather than join this time.
examples.zh: 知道想保留哪晚陪祖母，讓我對新承諾有較清楚方向。謝謝邀請，但這次我會留空那晚，不參加。

examples.en: I now have a clearer compass: I want to protect our regular evening together. The activity sounds interesting, but I cannot accept a commitment that falls at that time.
examples.zh: 我現有較清楚方向：想保留我們固定相聚的一晚。活動聽來有趣，但我不能接受剛好在那時的承諾。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用自己明確優先解釋接受或婉拒，不把方向清楚等同活動無價值，或要求他人採同一選擇。

takeaways.en: The mentor’s questions gave her a clearer compass for choosing a project that matched her values.
takeaways.zh: 導師的問題給她較清楚方向，選配合自身價值的項目。

takeaways.en: The residents’ request for easier access gave us a clearer compass for comparing the two entrance designs.
takeaways.zh: 居民要求較易進出，給我們比較兩種入口設計的較清楚方向。

brief.meaningEn: Have an emotional or thoughtful effect that continues after the immediate event.
brief.meaningZh: 當下事件過後，仍留下情感或思考上的影響。
brief.grammar: leave/leaves/left an echo; say what returns to the person’s thoughts or feelings; an echo is figurative here.
brief.register: Creative echo metaphor, not a claim that the whole phrase is a fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 持續迴盪不代表人人相同、永久影響或實際聲音反射；需有後續想法或感受的線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 與只記錄當刻聲音不同，也不由一人仍記得推所有人行為已改。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體後續感受表達餘韻，說清誰受到影響。

listening.en: The final question left an echo for me: on the bus home, I kept thinking about why the character had hidden the letter, even after our discussion had ended.
listening.zh: 最後問題對我留下餘韻：討論結束後，回家巴士上我仍在想人物為甚麼藏信。
listening.promptZh: echo 在這裏指甚麼？

options.en: The question continued to occupy the speaker’s thoughts after the discussion.
options.zh: 討論後，問題仍留在說話者思緒。

options.en: The speaker only remembered the wording while it was being read aloud.
options.zh: 說話者只在問題被朗讀時記得字句。

options.en: The group had already agreed on the character’s exact motive and no questions remained.
options.zh: 小組已同意人物確切動機，沒有餘下疑問。

options.en: The question returned to the speaker only when someone repeated the discussion word for word on the bus.
options.zh: 只有巴士上有人逐字重複討論，說話者才再想起問題。

listening.explanationZh: kept thinking及討論結束後回程，顯示思考自行延續；並沒說有人在巴士重複，亦未說動機已定。

reply.promptEn: Why did the final question stay with you on the way home?
reply.promptZh: 回家途中為甚麼仍記掛最後問題？

options.en: It made me keep considering the character’s hidden letter.
options.zh: 它令我繼續想人物藏信的事。

options.en: The discussion ended before my interest in the motive did.
options.zh: 討論結束，我對動機的興趣卻未停。

options.en: It left an echo because I was still thinking about the choice afterwards.
options.zh: 它留下餘韻，因為之後我仍在想那個選擇。

options.en: The unresolved question gave me something to reflect on beyond the session.
options.zh: 未解的問題讓我在環節後仍有內容反思。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都按本人後續思考，不改成全組已得同一答案。

scene.promptZh: 女作家讀完一封舊信，隔天選照片時仍想起信裏的體諒語氣，決定把同樣溫柔保留在說明中；沒有提實際回聲。哪句貼切？

options.en: The letter left an echo that shaped how she wanted to write the captions.
options.zh: 那封信留下餘韻，影響她想怎樣寫圖說。

options.en: She remembered nothing of the letter once she put it away.
options.zh: 放好信後，她已完全不記得內容。

options.en: The account is only about the volume of a voice in an empty room.
options.zh: 敘述只關乎空房裏說話的聲量。

scene.explanationZh: 隔天仍記語氣並影響寫法，是事件後的思緒延續。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持此處 leaves an echo？

options.en: Someone returns to a question after the conversation has ended.
options.zh: 談話完後，一個人仍反覆想某個問題。

options.en: A performance affects how a listener later thinks about a familiar memory.
options.zh: 演出影響聽者之後怎想一段熟悉回憶。

options.en: A sound is measured only for its volume, with no later thought or feeling described.
options.zh: 只量度聲音大小，沒交代後續想法或感受。

contrast.explanationZh: 這課的比喻需有延續影響，不是只有聲學量度。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把你自己的後續感受寫成「全場每人都永遠改變」；你只知道自己回程仍在想。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: The question left an echo for me, but I cannot describe everyone else’s later feelings.
options.zh: 問題對我留下餘韻，但我不能描述所有別人之後的感受。

options.en: The question stayed with our whole group on the way home, as my own journey shows.
options.zh: 從我自己的回程可見，問題回家路上一直留在整組人心裏。

options.en: I meant the excitement while we discussed the question, rather than a thought that continued afterwards.
options.zh: 我指討論問題當時的興奮，而非之後繼續的思考。

dialogue.explanationZh: 澄清只說本人事後延續的感受，不能由此推整組，也不能改成只有討論當時的興奮。

speaking.en: The story left an echo for me, and I found myself returning to its final question the next morning.
speaking.zh: 故事對我留下餘韻，翌早我發現自己仍在想最後問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用後續思考支持餘韻的比喻。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為短片配樂給意見，結尾旋律令你隔天走過舊碼頭時仍想起人物的離別。你想建議保留最後幾秒安靜，讓那段餘韻留下，不聲稱所有觀眾都會有同一回憶。用一至兩句英文回覆作曲者。

examples.en: Your closing melody left an echo for me; I thought of the farewell again when I passed the old pier the next day. Could we keep a few quiet seconds after it rather than cover the ending with another sound?
examples.zh: 你的結尾旋律對我留下餘韻；翌日經過舊碼頭，我又想起離別。可否保留之後幾秒安靜，而非用另一個聲音蓋住結尾？

examples.en: The music leaves an echo in my memory of the farewell, so I would leave a short silence at the end. That is my response, rather than a claim about what every viewer will remember.
examples.zh: 配樂在我對離別的記憶中留下餘韻，所以我會在結尾留短暫安靜。這是我的反應，不是聲稱每位觀眾會記起甚麼。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以翌日仍想起離別支持個人餘韻，提出具體配樂安排，不把自己的回憶當所有觀眾必然反應。

takeaways.en: Her final remark left an echo, and I returned to it while choosing the photographs later.
takeaways.zh: 她最後一句留下餘韻，之後選照片時我又想起。

takeaways.en: The reading leaves an echo for him long after the room has emptied, especially its question about belonging.
takeaways.zh: 大家離開房間後，那次朗讀仍對他留下餘韻，尤其是歸屬的問題。

brief.meaningEn: A small visible or known part of something substantially larger that remains hidden or unexamined.
brief.meaningZh: 已看見或知道的小部分，背後還有大得多、未顯露或未查清的情況。
brief.grammar: only/just/may be the tip of the iceberg; commonly problems, also a small known part of a larger hidden reality; qualify uncertain extent.
brief.register: Conventional idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是把任何小問題自動誇成巨大危機；需有更多情況的證據或清楚標示只是可能。
brief.misconceptionZh: 只看見一項不等於已知全貌，也不等於可替未查部分編數量。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出已知小部分及尚待調查的較大範圍，保留證據界限。

listening.en: The wrong label was the tip of the iceberg: checking the next shelf revealed a whole set of books filed under the old system, while the back room had not yet been inspected.
listening.zh: 錯標籤是冰山一角：查下一架發現一整批書仍按舊系統歸檔，後房還未檢查。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看待最初的錯標籤？

options.en: It was one visible sign of a wider filing problem that was not fully checked yet.
options.zh: 它是較廣歸檔問題的一個可見線索，尚未全查。

options.en: It was the only incorrect item, as every shelf and the back room had already been checked.
options.zh: 它是唯一錯項，因每架及後房已全部查過。

options.en: The new check showed that all the books had already moved to the new system.
options.zh: 新檢查顯示所有書已轉新系統。

options.en: The speaker already knew the exact total of affected books in every room.
options.zh: 說話者已知每間房受影響書籍的確切總數。

listening.explanationZh: 整批舊分類支持較廣問題，back room not yet inspected保留未知範圍，不編確切總數。

reply.promptEn: Why did you decide to check beyond the first wrong label?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼決定不只查首個錯標籤？

options.en: That label was the tip of the iceberg, with more old-system filing on the next shelf.
options.zh: 那標籤是冰山一角，下一架還有更多舊系統歸檔。

options.en: The next shelf showed that the issue extended beyond a single book.
options.zh: 下一架顯示不只一本有問題。

options.en: We had evidence of a wider problem, and the back room remained unchecked.
options.zh: 我們有較廣問題的證據，後房仍未查。

options.en: Fixing one label would not address the rest of the old filing we had found.
options.zh: 只改一標籤，未能處理已找到的其餘舊分類。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據已查到更多書，沒有假稱未知後房已全查。

scene.promptZh: 一張活動表只顯示某日借器材衝突，後來你查到其他四日也有未處理的重複預約，仍有一周要核。哪句貼切？

options.en: The first clash was the tip of the iceberg; more bookings need checking.
options.zh: 首個衝突是冰山一角；還有預約要核。

options.en: The first clash was a complete summary of every booking problem.
options.zh: 首個衝突已完整概括所有預約問題。

options.en: The remaining week has already been proved free of any duplicate booking.
options.zh: 餘下一周已證實沒有任何重複預約。

scene.explanationZh: 更多已知衝突支持小部分比喻，未核的一周仍不能定結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 the tip of the iceberg？

options.en: A first error leads to evidence of many related errors not yet fully explored.
options.zh: 首個錯誤帶出許多相關錯誤證據，尚未全查。

options.en: A complete check confirms one isolated error and no wider related issue.
options.zh: 完整核對確認只有一項獨立錯誤，沒有較廣相關問題。

options.en: A small public example is known to belong to a larger hidden pattern.
options.zh: 已知一個公開小例子屬於較大隱藏模式的一部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 明確孤立、已查清的一項，不符合背後大得多的未顯露範圍。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想在報告寫後房有「幾百本錯書」，但那裏未查；你已知下一架有一批。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: The first label was the tip of the iceberg, but we should inspect the back room before giving a total.
options.zh: 首標籤是冰山一角，但應查後房才給總數。

options.en: The number on the checked shelf should also be the confirmed total for the back room.
options.zh: 已查書架的數量，也應是後房已確認的總數。

options.en: I would finish the public report with the first label and wait to mention the next shelf until the total is available.
options.zh: 我會在公開報告只寫首個標籤，等有總數才提下一架。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已查書架的數量不能當未查後房確數；下一架已找到的情況可如實保留，不需等總數才承認。

speaking.en: The first error was the tip of the iceberg, so we checked the related records before deciding how much work was needed.
speaking.zh: 首個錯誤是冰山一角，所以我們先核相關紀錄，再判斷需做多少工作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把可見線索與較大待查範圍分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原以為社團活動只是台上兩小時。最近參與籌備，看見統籌安排輪值、查詢交通、逐一核無障礙需要，才明白公開環節只是可見小部分；你想請他列一項你可接手的後台工作，不假定已知道全部負擔。用一至兩句英文請求。

examples.en: The two-hour event was only the tip of the iceberg; I have now seen the rota planning and individual access checks behind it. Could you suggest one of those tasks that I could take on next time?
examples.zh: 兩小時活動只是冰山一角；我現看見背後輪值安排及個別無障礙需要核問。可否建議一項我下次能接手的工作？

examples.en: Seeing the transport enquiries showed me that the public session is the tip of the iceberg. I would like to help with a specific preparation task, rather than assume the whole workload ends when the audience leaves.
examples.zh: 看見交通查詢，讓我明白公開環節只是冰山一角。我想幫一項具體準備工作，而非假定觀眾離開便已全部完工。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以實際看見的幕後工作支持可見部分很小，提出有界限的參與，不編總量或假裝已知全部。

takeaways.en: The single missing form was the tip of the iceberg; the later audit uncovered a wider gap in the records.
takeaways.zh: 一張遺失表格是冰山一角；之後核查發現紀錄更大缺口。

takeaways.en: That unanswered booking may be the tip of the iceberg; we have found similar gaps in three other folders.
takeaways.zh: 那項未答預約可能是冰山一角；我們在另外三個文件夾找到類似缺漏。

target.pattern: \b(?:my|your|his|her|their|the) body is both (?:my|your|his|her|their|an) instrument and (?:my|your|his|her|their) livelihood\b

sources.expression: body is both their instrument and their livelihood
sources.sentence: For a dancer, the body is both their instrument and their livelihood.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page132, table1, row4; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: The body is both the means of performing skilled work and the basis of earning a living.
brief.meaningZh: 身體既是完成專業表現的工具，也是賺取生活收入所依靠的根本。
brief.grammar: For a performer, their body is both their instrument and their livelihood; keep pronouns consistent; both...and... names two connected roles.
brief.register: Extended body-as-instrument metaphor with a natural livelihood connection.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是每個用身體活動的人都以此謀生；需有工作及收入線索，也不由此推人人應採同一安排。
brief.misconceptionZh: 工具比喻強調表現媒介，livelihood強調生計，不能只看到愛好而漏掉職業層面。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以人物職業說明技能表現與生活收入的連結。

listening.en: For the freelance dancer, her body is both her instrument and her livelihood: movement is how she creates the work, and paid performances cover her living costs, so rehearsal plans affect more than a hobby.
listening.zh: 對自由身舞者而言，身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫：她以動作創作，靠有酬演出支付生活，排練安排不只是愛好問題。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼同時提 instrument 和 livelihood？

options.en: The dancer uses movement to create her work and earns her living through performances.
options.zh: 舞者以動作創作，也靠演出維持生活。

options.en: The dancer only attends unpaid classes as an occasional hobby.
options.zh: 舞者只偶爾上無酬課，當作愛好。

options.en: The dancer earns all her income from selling musical instruments.
options.zh: 舞者全部收入都來自出售樂器。

options.en: The speaker says rehearsal plans cannot affect her working life.
options.zh: 說話者說排練安排不可能影響她的職業生活。

listening.explanationZh: creates the work及paid performances分別支持兩個角色，不是只有興趣或字面樂器。

reply.promptEn: Why do rehearsal arrangements matter beyond the dancer’s enjoyment?
reply.promptZh: 排練安排為甚麼不只關乎舞者的樂趣？

options.en: Her movement is the medium of her work, and the performances pay her living costs.
options.zh: 動作是她工作的媒介，演出支付生活費。

options.en: Her body is both her instrument and her livelihood.
options.zh: 她的身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫。

options.en: The work joins artistic expression with the income she depends on.
options.zh: 這工作把藝術表現與她依靠的收入連起來。

options.en: Decisions about performing also matter for how she earns a living.
options.zh: 表演決定也影響她怎樣賺取生活。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留專業表現及收入兩層，沒有把她改成只玩興趣。

scene.promptZh: 一位女舞者周末無酬表演，以動作創作，但全部生活收入來自平日翻譯工作。你想準確區分表演媒介與生計來源。哪句符合資料？

options.en: Her body is an instrument for the performance, but this account does not make it her livelihood.
options.zh: 身體是她表演的工具，但這敘述沒有把它說成生計來源。

options.en: Her body is both her instrument and her livelihood because she performs at weekends.
options.zh: 因她周末演出，身體便既是表演工具，也是生計所繫。

options.en: The translation income shows that she uses words rather than movement in the performance.
options.zh: 翻譯收入顯示她演出時用文字，而非動作。

scene.explanationZh: 無酬動作表演支持媒介角色，生活收入卻另來自翻譯；不能把參與表演就當靠它謀生。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 body is both their instrument and their livelihood？

options.en: A paid dancer relies on bodily movement to create performances and earn income.
options.zh: 有酬舞者依靠身體動作創作演出並賺取收入。

options.en: An unpaid hobbyist enjoys an occasional movement class but earns their living elsewhere.
options.zh: 無酬愛好者偶爾上動作課，另以其他工作謀生。

options.en: A professional performer’s physical skills underpin work that pays their living costs.
options.zh: 專業表演者的身體技巧，支撐支付生活費的工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 愛好可有身體表現，卻未提供livelihood所需的謀生連結。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把舞者排練說成可隨意取消的休閒活動；你知道她靠演出收入生活。哪句澄清較準確？

options.en: Her body is both her instrument and her livelihood, so we should discuss the working arrangements rather than treat them as a casual hobby.
options.zh: 她的身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫，所以應商量工作安排，而非當隨意愛好。

options.en: The rehearsals sound optional until ticket income arrives, so we could decide their times after the paid dates are fixed.
options.zh: 排練聽來在票款到前都屬可選，可等有酬演出日期定後才定時間。

options.en: I thought the fees covered the performances only, so the preparation time did not belong in the work discussion.
options.zh: 我以為酬勞只付演出，所以準備時間不屬工作安排討論。

dialogue.explanationZh: 表演媒介及生計相連，排練與實際工作安排相關；不能只因未收票款或酬勞列在演出，就把準備當純休閒。

speaking.en: For a professional dancer, their body is both their instrument and their livelihood, so working arrangements deserve careful discussion.
speaking.zh: 對專業舞者而言，身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫，所以工作安排值得仔細商量。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出創作工具與謀生兩個角色。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你是自由身肢體劇演員，製作人臨時加一場演出，但尚未談新增排練時間與酬勞。你靠動作創作，也靠有酬演出維持生活；想在答應前商量這些安排，不提出訓練或醫療建議。用一至兩句英文直接回覆製作人。

examples.en: My body is both my instrument and my livelihood, so I need to discuss the added rehearsal time and fee before agreeing to another performance. Could we review those arrangements together?
examples.zh: 身體既是我的表演工具，也是生計所繫，所以答應另一場前需商量新增排練時間及酬勞。可否一起檢視安排？

examples.en: Because my body is both my instrument and my livelihood, an extra performance is a work commitment for me. I would like to agree the preparation time and payment with you before I accept.
examples.zh: 身體既是我的表演工具，也是生計所繫，所以額外一場是工作承諾。我想接受前先與你議好準備時間及酬勞。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以創作媒介及有酬工作說明需協商的時間和酬勞，回覆製作人而非描述文章應怎寫，不替對方假定條件。

takeaways.en: As a paid movement artist, my body is both my instrument and my livelihood; the work joins expression and earning a living.
takeaways.zh: 作為有酬動作藝術家，我的身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫；工作連結表現及謀生。

takeaways.en: For the touring dancer, their body is both their instrument and their livelihood, not merely a way to enjoy a spare afternoon.
takeaways.zh: 對巡演舞者而言，身體既是表演工具，也是生計所繫，不只是享受空閒下午的方法。

sources.sentence: The captain stayed calm when it matters most.
sources.locatorNote: Actual PDF page132, table1, row5; unreported locators remain null.

brief.meaningEn: At the point when the action or response is especially important to the outcome.
brief.meaningZh: 在行動或回應對結果特別重要的時刻。
brief.grammar: when it matters most / when it mattered most; it refers to contextual importance, not necessarily a separate concrete object.
brief.register: Common time-and-importance expression.
brief.boundaryZh: most表示情境中的重要關頭，不等於最晚、最大聲或每次都成功；時態需配合敘事。
brief.misconceptionZh: 說清為何那時重要，不能只加most便製造關鍵性。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出重要時點及有用回應，保留具體情境。

listening.en: The rehearsal was calm, but when the live question confused the guests, the interpreter helped when it mattered most: she clarified the unfamiliar term before anyone acted on the wrong instruction.
listening.zh: 排練平靜，但現場問題令來賓困惑時，傳譯員在重要關頭幫忙：她趕在大家按錯指示行動前，澄清陌生詞。
listening.promptZh: 為甚麼那一刻特別重要？

options.en: Clarifying the term prevented people from acting on a misunderstood instruction.
options.zh: 澄清詞語，避免大家按誤解的指示行動。

options.en: It was the latest possible minute on the programme, regardless of what guests understood.
options.zh: 不管來賓是否明白，那只是流程最晚一分鐘。

options.en: The interpreter was only revising notes after every guest had already left.
options.zh: 傳譯員只在所有來賓離開後改筆記。

options.en: The interpreter’s useful clarification came during the rehearsal, while the live confusion remained unresolved.
options.zh: 傳譯員有用的澄清在排練時發生，現場困惑仍未解。

listening.explanationZh: 澄清發生在現場、誤解尚未變行動時，故影響重要；不是只在排練或來賓離開後。

reply.promptEn: Why was the interpreter’s clarification so valuable at that moment?
reply.promptZh: 傳譯員的澄清，為甚麼當時特別有價值？

options.en: People needed to understand before following the instruction.
options.zh: 大家按指示做之前，需先明白。

options.en: She caught a misunderstanding at a point when it could affect what guests did next.
options.zh: 她在誤解會影響來賓下一步的時點發現問題。

options.en: She helped when it mattered most, before the wrong action was taken.
options.zh: 她在最重要關頭幫忙，趕在錯誤行動前。

options.en: The timely explanation connected the unfamiliar term with the action people were about to take.
options.zh: 及時解釋，連起陌生詞及大家即將作的行動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代為何時點重要，不只換成較晚或較響亮。

scene.promptZh: 小組演出前，一位成員發現出口指示與當晚座位安排不符，及時請負責人修正，觀眾尚未進場。哪句貼切？

options.en: She spoke up when it mattered most, while there was still time to correct the signs.
options.zh: 她在重要關頭開口，當時仍來得及改標牌。

options.en: Her comment mattered only because she waited until no one could change the signs.
options.zh: 她的意見只因等到沒人能改標牌才重要。

options.en: She was discussing a past event with no effect on tonight’s arrangements.
options.zh: 她只談過去活動，對今晚安排沒影響。

scene.explanationZh: 觀眾進場前可改且影響安排，支持重要時點，不是最晚才有用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論最不宜由 when it matters most 得出？

options.en: The context identifies a particularly consequential moment.
options.zh: 情境指出一個對結果特別有影響的時刻。

options.en: The phrase must mean the last minute, whether or not anything important depends on it.
options.zh: 它一定指最後一分鐘，不管是否有重要事情取決於當時。

options.en: An action may be valuable because it occurs before a consequential choice.
options.zh: 行動可因發生在重要選擇之前而有價值。

contrast.explanationZh: 重要程度取決於情境，不等同固定鐘點或越遲越好。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友以為這表達鼓勵凡事拖到最後；你談的是來賓行動前的及時澄清。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Helping when it matters most is about the importance of the moment, not waiting as long as possible.
options.zh: 在重要關頭幫忙，是看時點的重要性，不是盡量拖延。

options.en: Then the same help would matter most at the end of the programme, even if the guests had already chosen what to do.
options.zh: 那麼即使來賓已決定行動，同一幫助仍應在流程最後最重要。

options.en: I took it to mean the most impressive part of her speech, rather than the moment the guests needed clarification.
options.zh: 我理解成她演說最精彩部分，而非來賓需澄清的時點。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需用當時需要及影響解釋重要性；不是固定流程最後，也不只是演說最精彩部分。

speaking.en: She asked the careful question when it mattered most, before the group committed to a plan it had misunderstood.
speaking.zh: 小組答應自己誤解的計劃前，她在重要關頭仔細提問。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清那一刻為何重要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你決定是否回校完成停下的課程時，朋友沒有替你選，卻陪你整理最在意的理由。你後來自行決定回去，想寫謝訊，說這種陪伴在你面對重要抉擇時特別有用；不說他保證結果。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: You listened when it mattered most, while I was deciding whether to return to the course. Thank you for helping me sort out my reasons without choosing for me.
examples.zh: 我決定是否回課程時，你在重要關頭聆聽。謝謝你幫我整理理由，卻沒有替我選。

examples.en: Your patient questions helped when it mattered most: I needed to understand what returning would mean to me. I made the decision myself, but I appreciated having you beside me.
examples.zh: 你的耐心問題在重要關頭幫了我：我需明白重返課程對自己的意義。決定是我自己作，但我珍惜你在身旁。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以重大抉擇所需的聆聽支持說明重要時點，保留自己決定與結果未知，不一定要拖到最後一刻。

takeaways.en: He explained the unfamiliar rule when it mattered most, just before the newcomers began the task.
takeaways.zh: 新人開始任務前，他在重要關頭解釋陌生規則。

takeaways.en: His quiet question helped when it mattered most, before we sent an invitation with the wrong date.
takeaways.zh: 寄出日期錯的邀請前，他安靜的提問在重要關頭幫了忙。
